P1.evidence: The only call in this batch where the application was read back, and it was done three times: 'I read, if I'm correct, that you're 35, right?', 'I also read that you sort of put down that if you don't change, like now, it's going to be harder and harder', and 'I also read that you want to have, like, a balanced body.' That is exactly what P1a asks for. The frame was the thinnest version he ran all week, however — 'go into what you would like to achieve through us, see if we can help you with that. If not, I'll point you in the right direction' — two parts plus the disqualification clause, with no 'where you are' and no 'what's in the way'. No agreement was sought at all; he went straight from the frame into the open question, which itself ran cleanly.

P2.evidence: Age, height and weight were all obtained directly and early. Current training frequency was established well — four times a week now, and a stated capacity for four to five sessions. Diet was properly probed and produced a specific picture: vegetarian, struggling with satiety, using grains, fruit, fibre and chia seeds. Everything else was missed. Occupation was never asked, which is remarkable given that being a professional dancer and movement teacher is the single most important fact about this prospect and determined the entire outcome; it surfaced only because he volunteered it in his first answer. Health conditions were never asked, so functional scoliosis arrived unprompted and was never followed up. Injuries, pain and movement limitations were never asked either — the hypermobility, weak adductors and posterior pelvic tilt difficulty all came out in response to a mobility question rather than a baseline one. Sleep and energy were both absent.

P3.evidence: The front half ran and the back half did not. The specific-goal question was asked well — 'Do you have like any specific goals as in losing fat amounts, gaining muscle mass?' — and produced a genuinely useful answer about valuing skill and load progression over composition. The mobility and flexibility question produced the most important disclosures in the call. The bridge to the deeper why was asked twice and properly: 'a lot of times people have a deeper why for wanting to actually work on their physical... do you think you have somewhat of a deeper why for yourself?' It returned nothing, and the prospect pushed back on the whole line of enquiry — 'I think the conversation is getting like a little like metaphysical' and 'I'm pretty content with my body performance in my field.' The rep respected that, which is defensible, but he then made no further attempt: the impact question, the who-else question and the drive through to identity or legacy were never asked in any form. Two accurate reflect-backs did run with confirmation.

P4.evidence: The strongest phase of the call and efficiently run. The pattern was established clearly — 'I always drop off after like a few weeks and then you start from ground zero again, always with strength training, never get to that point of progressing' — and when the rep asked the root-cause question, 'Why not do you think so?', he got a clean and unusually self-aware answer: 'Because I don't enjoy it, so then I don't like spending time on it.' The prospect then named the gap himself with real force: 'from day one, I was not interested in other strength training. And I've always been intrigued about kettlebells... So it's no wonder why I'm not consistent, you know?' That is the single most useful piece of information in the call, and the rep elicited it. Marked down because past attempts beyond the gym were never broadly canvassed, and the 'why can't you stick to it on your own?' challenge was never put — though it was arguably redundant once enjoyment had been isolated as the mechanism.

P5.evidence: Entirely absent. There is no two-year projection, no settle question, no 'why not', and no line in the sand anywhere in the thirty-two minutes. The nearest thing is 'when did you make the decision for yourself that you do want to make a change like that?', which is a trigger question and belongs to a different phase. The application had even handed the rep the raw material — he read out that the prospect had written that changing later would get harder — and that thread was never picked up. With no cost of inaction established, nothing was holding the value case together when the product gap surfaced.

P6.evidence: Per-pillar commitment checks were attempted but none of them landed, because the prospect deflected every one back to the same unanswered question. After the training pillar: 'Oh, yeah, that's fine. I'm still just not understanding, like, the clear, like, packages.' After nutrition: 'I mean, once again, it gets back to, like, the package.' The all-in isolation question was never asked. P6c is the decisive failure — the script requires a clear yes before presenting anything, and the rep never had one at any point, yet delivered the full presentation regardless. When he finally did gate the price behind a commitment check at 00:28:54, the answer was an immediate no: 'I don't see the value in the individualized one for myself.' That answer was available fifteen minutes earlier had the question been asked.

P11.evidence: Both prices were presented and the prospect declined both immediately, so no payment or onboarding step was reachable. Scored not applicable rather than miss, consistent with the other clean losses in this batch.

objection_plays.detail: Script gap and the defining issue of this call. The prospect stated his requirement in his first substantive answer — technique check-ins and form correction, without daily accountability — and clarified at 00:13:28 that he pictured 'a weekly or once every other week private session. And then that's the technique, that's the check-in, and then I'm doing the rest of the program myself.' Neither tier offers live synchronous coaching; the rep confirmed this only at 00:28:38 ('He does jump on and sometimes on with clients, but overall it's not something we do every month, every week') and again at 00:30:08 ('No, not really'). The playbook has no disqualification path for a stated requirement the product cannot meet, so the rep ran the full presentation against a need he could not serve. His manager identified the correct move in a coaching session the same afternoon — 'it sounds like you want a personal trainer, and honestly, that's just not what we do' — and the rep acknowledged there that he had 'pitched for the sake of pitching'.

Second script gap. The prospect asked for package structure and price six times across fifteen minutes — at 00:14:41, 00:15:42, 00:19:14, 00:25:00, 00:27:27 and 00:28:47 — with increasing directness, ending in 'so then what is the financial investment difference between the non-customized and the customized?' Each request was deflected so the presentation could continue, and the final one was answered with a commitment check rather than a number. The playbook contains no guidance for a prospect who wants the commercial terms early, and no permitted way to give a price before the presentation is complete, so a reasonable buyer request read as an obstacle to be managed.

notes: Past Attempts was excellent — he isolated enjoyment as the mechanism behind years of failed strength training, which is the real insight in this call. Everything else was governed by not listening to the opening answer. The prospect said in his first minute that he did not want daily accountability and wanted form checks before weight progression; the rep steered him toward the premium one-to-one tier anyway, skipped the Consequence Frame entirely, never obtained a yes at the commitment check, and deflected six direct requests for pricing to protect the script. Coach on disqualifying early when a stated requirement is outside the product, and on answering a direct pricing question the first time it is asked.
